detail.backupPathsDescription: Add backup paths here that are to be saved in the backup repository.
detail.dbDumpPathHelpText: Directory the database dump is written to before it gets pushed into the backup repository. A path starting with a slash is used as an absolute path, any other value is resolved against the shop directory. Leave empty to use the default path var/db/backup. Beware: the directory gets emptied completely before and after every database backup.
detail.forgetDescription: Specify here the deletion of snapshots that are older than the specified number of days.
detail.repositoryPathDescription: The path to the backup repository. Enter here the absolute path to the backup repository. Note that this path cannot be changed after creation!
detail.repositoryPasswordDescription: Remembering this password is very important! If you lose it, you won’t be able to get access to the data stored in the repository outside of the shop functionality. Note that this path cannot be changed after creation!
detail.statsHistoryEmptyTitle: No entries in the selected period
detail.statsEmptySubline: The status is collected at the end of every backup run. Alternatively via CLI: bin/console muckiware:repository:stats <id>

pathField.loadError: The folder could not be loaded.
pathField.invalidPath: Invalid path or folder not readable

dumpPath.rootDirectory: The root directory cannot be used as dump path. The backup uses the default path var/db/backup instead.
dumpPath.relativeSegment: The path must not contain "." or ".." segments. The backup uses the default path var/db/backup instead.
dumpPath.projectDirOrParent: The shop directory or one of its parent directories cannot be used as dump path. The backup uses the default path var/db/backup instead.
dumpPath.overlapsRepositoryOrRestorePath: The dump path overlaps with the repository path or the restore path. The backup uses the default path var/db/backup instead.
dumpPath.blockedPath: This directory is protected and cannot be used as dump path. The backup uses the default path var/db/backup instead.
dumpPath.notWritable: The folder (or its nearest existing parent folder) is not writable for the web server user. The backup may fall back to the default path var/db/backup.
